parts.text: A student investigates the image formed by a converging lens. Refer to Fig. 3.1.

parts.label: a
parts.text: (a) The student: • switches on the lamp • places the screen a distance D = 80.0 cm from the illuminated object (a triangular hole in a piece of card) • places the lens close to the illuminated object • moves the lens away from the illuminated object until a magnified, inverted, sharp image of the illuminated object is formed on the screen. Fig. 3.1 shows the position of the lens when the image is sharp. Fig. 3.1

parts.label: i
parts.text: (i) On Fig. 3.1, measure, to the nearest 0.1 cm, the object distance x from the centre of the lens to the illuminated object. x = ................................................... cm [1]

parts.label: ii
parts.text: (ii) Fig. 3.1 is drawn to a scale of one-fifth full size. Calculate the actual object distance X. X = ................................................... cm [1]

parts.label: b
parts.text: (b) The student: • continues to move the lens away from the illuminated object until a second sharp image, which is diminished and inverted, is formed on the screen • measures, to the nearest 0.1 cm, the object distance Y from the centre of the lens to the illuminated object. 59.8 cm Y = ...............................................................

parts.label: i
parts.text: (i) Fig. 3.2 shows the illuminated object. On Fig. 3.2, draw a diminished, inverted image in the space provided. Fig. 3.2 [1]

parts.label: c
parts.text: (c) The focal length f of the lens can be found using the equation: f = (D 2 – d 2 ) 4D . Use the value of D from (a) and d from (b)(ii) to calculate a value f 1 for the focal length of the lens. Give your answer to 3 significant figures. f 1 = ................................................... cm [2]

parts.label: e
parts.text: (e) Two quantities can be considered to be equal within the limits of experimental accuracy if their values are within 10% of each other. State whether your values of f 1 and f 2 from (c) and (d) can be considered equal. Support your statement with a calculation. statement .................................................................................................................................. ................................................................................................................................................... [2]

ms.label: 3(e)
ms.text:
statement to match results (expect YES)
values used in a calculation to justify the statement

ms.label: 3(f)(i)
ms.text: move the lens slowly / backwards and forwards

ms.label: 3(f)(ii)
ms.text: better contrast between the image and the rest of the screen / edges of the image are sharper / more visible / easier to view
